clocks.name: Annus Mundi
clocks.formula: Era count, years elapsed since 3895 BC. JS: am = astro + 3894 (astro = astronomical year, 1 BC = 0). Source comment also: AM = 3895 - (BC year). Anchors: 2022 CE -> 5916; 2239 BC -> 1656; 2026 -> 5920; AM 6000 = 2106 CE. Flag: isPalindrome(am).
clocks.description: The Ancient-World count from the 3895 BC poleshift - the calendar's Year One. Flood node AM 1656; AM 6000 in 2106 CE.

clocks.name: Cataclysm Era
clocks.formula: Years since the Nemesis Cataclysm of 5239 BC. JS: cat = astro + 5238. Meta note: 7-cycle Nemesis frame = 5544 yr (792x7).
clocks.description: Years since the Nemesis Cataclysm of 5239 BC, when the binary broke apart.

clocks.name: Phoenix · Sky Dragon
clocks.formula: Strict 138-yr lattice; node where mod(astro,138) === 108; node #1 = 4309 BC (PHX = {mod:108, step:138, base:-4308}). JS: pPrev = astro - mod(astro-108,138); pNext = pPrev + 138; pInto = astro - pPrev; pTo = pNext - astro; pIdx = Math.round((pPrev - PHX.base)/138) + 1; bar = pInto/138*100. mod(n,m) = ((n%m)+m)%m. Multiples: 138x3=414 'cursed time', 138x4=552 'Phoenix cycles', 138x46=6348 (4309 BC -> 2040 CE).
clocks.description: The 138-year reset cycle - the recurring destroyer Breshears named; due 15 May 2040. Node #1 = 4309 BC; nodes 1902, 2040, 2178.

clocks.name: Nemesis X Object
clocks.formula: 792-yr orbit: enters inner system when mod(astro-462,792) === 0, inside for 60 yr, outside 732 yr (NEM_ENTER = {mod:462, step:792}). JS: offset = mod(astro-462,792); inner = offset < 60; enterPrev = astro - offset; enterNext = enterPrev + 792; exit = enterPrev + 60; if inner: yrsLeft = 60 - offset, bar = offset/60*100; else: yrsToReturn = enterNext - astro, bar = (astro - (enterPrev+60))/732*100. Ledger marker: txt uses offset<60, v2 uses offset<=60.
clocks.description: The 792-year orbit of the dark companion - 60 yr inside Sol, 732 without; returns 2046.

clocks.name: Anunnaki NER
clocks.formula: 600-yr epochs phased on astro 162 (NER = {mod:162, step:600, base:-5238}; 5239 BC start). JS: nerOff = mod(astro-162,600); nerStart = astro - nerOff; nerNum = Math.floor((astro - NER.base)/600) + 1; next = nerStart + 600; bar = nerOff/600*100. Each 600-yr NER = ten 60-yr decans. 762 CE = 6000th NER year.
clocks.description: The 600-year regnal epochs of the Anunna kings - ten 60-year decans apiece. 762 CE falls on the 6000th NER year.

clocks.name: Mayan Long-Count
clocks.formula: Hard-coded baktun boundaries MAY_NODES = [-3112,-2712,-2312,-1912,-1512,-1112,-712,-318,76,470,864,1258,1652,2046] (six 400-yr spans, then seven 394-yr spans after -712). Find bi with MAY_NODES[bi] <= astro < MAY_NODES[bi+1]; label 'BAKTUN '+(bi+1)+'/13'; span = bEnd - bStart; into = astro - bStart; yrsToNext = bEnd - astro; before -3112 = PRE-COUNT; v2: astro >= 2046 -> '13.0.0.0.0 complete'. Long-Count year: lc = astro + 3112 (2026 -> 5138; 2046 -> 5158). Sigil flag (v2): lc > 0 && String(lc).indexOf('138') >= 0.
clocks.description: Thirteen baktuns of 144,000 days from 3113 BC, closing at 13.0.0.0.0 in 2046. 2026 = LC 5138.

clocks.name: Lunar Clock · Metonic recursion
clocks.formula: 19 yr = 235 lunations (235/19 = 12.368 moons/yr). Flag: mod(REF - astro, 19) === 0 where REF = 2026 (txt) or TODAY.y (v2). Cycle count: yd = REF - astro; yd >= 0 ? Math.floor(yd/19)+' back' : Math.abs(Math.floor(yd/19))+' ahead'.
clocks.description: The 19-year Metonic gear - after 235 lunations the moon returns to the same phase on the same date.

clocks.name: Moon phase (continuous synodic model)
clocks.formula: SYN = 29.530588853; NEWMOON_J2000 = 2451550.1 (2000-01-06 18:14 UT). J = jdn(astro,m,d) (proleptic Gregorian: a=floor((14-m)/12); y=astro+4800-a; mm=m+12a-3; J = d+floor((153mm+2)/5)+365y+floor(y/4)-floor(y/100)+floor(y/400)-32045). age = mod(J - NEWMOON_J2000, SYN); frac = age/SYN; illum = (1-cos(2*PI*frac))/2; phaseIdx = floor(mod(frac+1/16,1)*8)%8 over [New, Waxing Crescent, First Quarter, Waxing Gibbous, Full, Waning Gibbous, Last Quarter, Waning Crescent]; lunation (txt) = Math.round((J-2423436.40347)/SYN), (v2) = Math.floor((J-2423436.40347)/SYN)+1; moonsFromToday = Math.round((TODAY_JD - J)/SYN).
clocks.description: Moon age, illumination and lunation number from a J2000 new-moon epoch; deep-past phases are cycle-true rather than historically observed.

clocks.name: Anunna Reckoning · šar = a turning of the stars
clocks.formula: šar = one day (a turning). JS: AM_EPOCH = jdn(-3894,1,1); turns = J - AM_EPOCH; T = |turns|; Draconian yr = T/360; NER = T/216000; baktun = T/144000; nodes: T===432000 'antediluvian total', T===864000 'Foundation of Time', T%144000===0 'n x baktun'. 432,000 = 3 baktuns = 1,200 Draconian yr; 864,000 = 6 baktuns = 2,400 Draconian yr; Enoch 300 yr = 108,000 turnings.
clocks.description: Counts turnings (days) since AM Year One, 3895 BC, read in Draconian measures: 360 = 1 Draconian yr, 216,000 = 1 NER, 144,000 = 1 baktun.

clocks.name: Phoenix Countdown · 15 May 2040
clocks.formula: Live: ms = Date.UTC(2040,4,15,0,0,0) - now; days = floor(ms/86400000); flags days%138===0 '÷138 today', days%19===0 '÷19 today'; also yrsTo(y) = ((Date.UTC(y,0,1)-Date.now())/3.15576e10).toFixed(1) for 2046 and 2178. After target: 'ARRIVED'.
clocks.description: Live count to the 2040 reset - calls it out whenever the days remaining fall on a multiple of 19 or 138.

clocks.name: Giza Apparent Solar · the true sun
clocks.formula: lon = 31.1342; utcH = h + m/60 + s/3600; B = 2*PI*(dayOfYear-81)/364; EoT = 9.87*sin(2B) - 7.53*cos(B) - 1.5*sin(B) (minutes); solarH = ((utcH + lon/15 + EoT/60) % 24 + 24) % 24.
clocks.description: Sundial time over the pyramid's own meridian, corrected by the equation of time.

clocks.name: Cairo · Giza Plateau
clocks.formula: Intl.DateTimeFormat timeZone 'Africa/Cairo'; offset read from shortOffset (default 2); label EEST if UTC+3 else EET. Meta: 30.0°N 31.1°E.
clocks.description: Civil time where the Great Pyramid stands - the stone this whole instrument reads.

clocks.name: UTC · Zulu
clocks.formula: now.getUTCHours/Minutes/Seconds.
clocks.description: Coordinated Universal Time - the world's reference clock.

clocks.name: Your meridian · local
clocks.formula: now.getHours/Minutes/Seconds; zone from Intl resolvedOptions().timeZone.
clocks.description: This device's own time zone, wherever you are reading from.

clocks.name: Solar Year · day-length
clocks.formula: leap = (astro%4===0) && (astro%100!==0 || astro%400===0); days = leap ? 366 : 365. Note: the Draconian/Anunna year was 360 turnings.
clocks.description: Length of the dialed year - 365 or 366; the Anunna/Draconian year was 360.

clocks.name: Hebrew · Anno Mundi
clocks.formula: hy = Intl year (calendar 'hebrew'); metonicYr = mod(hy,19) || 19; leap13 = mod(7*hy+1,19) < 7; hgap = (astro+3894) - hy (Archaix AM minus Hebrew AM; flagged when hgap%19===0). Epoch stated as 3761 BC, 134 yr after Year One (133 after Rosh Hashanah).
clocks.description: Rabbinic world-era, built on the same 19-year Metonic gear as the moon.

clocks.name: Coptic · Church of Egypt
clocks.formula: Intl calendar 'coptic' (year = first digit-run). Year of the Martyrs from 284 CE.
clocks.description: The Egyptian church's count from the Year of the Martyrs, 284 CE.

clocks.name: Egyptian Civil · Nabonassar
clocks.formula: ed = J - 1448638; year = floor(ed/365)+1; doy = mod(ed,365); month = floor(doy/30) (Thoth..Mesore, 12 x 30) else epagomenae; day = mod(doy,30)+1.
clocks.description: The ancient 365-day wandering year that drifts a full turn every Sothic 1460.

clocks.name: Sothic cycle
clocks.formula: v2: sothicPos = mod(astro - 139, 1460) + '/1460'. MANUAL constant OPH_SOTHIC = 1461 (years), no position formula.
clocks.description: The Egyptian civil year drifts a full turn every Sothic 1460 (v2). MANUAL lists OPH_SOTHIC = 1461 years.

clocks.name: Mayan Calendar Round
clocks.formula: ld = J - 584283; tzolkin = (mod(ld+3,13)+1) + ' ' + tzNm[mod(ld+19,20)]; hp = mod(ld+348,365); haabMonth = floor(hp/20) (Pop..Kumku, 18) else Wayeb; haabDay = mod(hp,20). Round 52 yr / 18,980 d (260-day Tzolkin x 365-day Haab).
clocks.description: The 52-year meshing of the 260-day Tzolkin and 365-day Haab.

clocks.name: Julian Calendar · Old Style
clocks.formula: fromJDJulian(J): c=J+32082; d=floor((4c+3)/1461); e=c-floor(1461d/4); m=floor((5e+2)/153); day=e-floor((153m+2)/5)+1; month=m+3-12*floor(m/10); year=d-4800+floor(m/10). gap = J - jdn(julian y,m,d) days behind Gregorian.
clocks.description: Caesar's calendar - now 13 days behind Gregorian.

clocks.name: Julian Day · raw count
clocks.formula: J = jdn(astro,m,d) (proleptic Gregorian JDN, see lunar-synodic). Flags palindromic day; next palindrome JDN.
clocks.description: The astronomer's continuous day-number since 4713 BC.

clocks.name: Islamic · Hijri
clocks.formula: Intl calendar 'islamic'.
clocks.description: The Muslim lunar year, ~354 days, from 622 CE.

clocks.name: Persian · Solar Hijri
clocks.formula: Intl calendar 'persian'. Meta: 'from 622 CE'.
clocks.description: The most astronomically accurate solar calendar in use.

clocks.name: Indian National · Saka
clocks.formula: Intl calendar 'indian'.
clocks.description: India's civil calendar, epoch 78 CE.

clocks.name: Buddhist Era
clocks.formula: be = astro + 543.
clocks.description: Theravada count - CE + 543.

clocks.name: Ethiopic
clocks.formula: Intl calendar 'ethiopic' (Amete Mihret).
clocks.description: Thirteen months, ~7-8 years behind Gregorian.

clocks.name: Chinese · sexagenary
clocks.formula: ci = mod(astro-4,60); stem = st[mod(ci,10)] (Jia..Gui); branch = br[mod(ci,12)] (Zi..Hai); element = el[mod(ci,10)]; animal = an[mod(ci,12)]; yr = ci+1 of 60; 'approx at Jan'.
clocks.description: The 60-year cycle of stem, branch, element and zodiac animal.

clocks.name: Byzantine · Old Russian
clocks.formula: year = m >= 9 ? astro + 5509 : astro + 5508.
clocks.description: The creation world-era from 1 Sept 5509 BC.

clocks.name: Kali Yuga · Vedic
clocks.formula: ky = astro + 3101.
clocks.description: The Hindu dark age, begun 3102 BC.

clocks.name: Holocene · Human Era
clocks.formula: he = astro + 10000.
clocks.description: CE + 10,000 - counting from the dawn of settlement.

clocks.name: French Republican
clocks.formula: fJD = J - 2375839; if fJD < 1 'pre-Republic'; fy = floor((fJD-1)/365.2422)+1; fdoy = floor(fJD-1-(fy-1)*365.2422); month = floor(fdoy/30) (Vendemiaire..Fructidor) else Sansculottides; day = mod(fdoy,30)+1. Approximate.
clocks.description: The Revolution's decimal calendar of 1793 (approximate).

clocks.name: Unix · machine time
clocks.formula: ux = Math.round(dt.getTime()/1000).
clocks.description: Seconds elapsed since 1 Jan 1970.

clocks.name: Saros eclipse cycle
clocks.formula: Constant only: OPH_SAROS = 6585.3211 days (18.03 years). No epoch or position formula in the sources.
clocks.description: The Saros eclipse cycle, in days (18.03 years). Natorion equation constant.

clocks.name: Inex eclipse cycle
clocks.formula: Constant only: OPH_INEX = 10571.95 days (28.94 years). No epoch or position formula.
clocks.description: The Inex eclipse cycle, in days (28.94 years). Natorion equation constant.

clocks.name: Precession of the equinoxes
clocks.formula: Constant only: OPH_PRECESSION = 25772 years. v2 prose: '72 years - one precessional degree'. No epoch or position formula.
clocks.description: One precession of the equinoxes, in years (MANUAL). v2 prose calls 72 years one precessional degree.

clocks.name: Jupiter-Saturn great conjunction
clocks.formula: Constant only: OPH_JUPSAT = 19.86 years.
clocks.description: Jupiter-Saturn great conjunction, in years. Natorion equation constant.

clocks.name: Jupiter return
clocks.formula: Constant only: OPH_JUPITER = 11.862 years.
clocks.description: Jupiter return, in years. Natorion equation constant.

clocks.name: Saturn return
clocks.formula: Constant only: OPH_SATURN = 29.4571 years.
clocks.description: Saturn return, in years. Natorion equation constant.

clocks.name: Uranus return
clocks.formula: Constant only: OPH_URANUS = 84.0205 years.
clocks.description: Uranus return, in years. Natorion equation constant.

clocks.name: Chiron return
clocks.formula: Constant only: OPH_CHIRON = 50.42 years.
clocks.description: Chiron return, in years. Natorion equation constant.

clocks.name: Year lengths (tropical / sidereal / anomalistic / ideal)
clocks.formula: Constants only: OPH_YEAR_TROPICAL = 365.24219 d; OPH_YEAR_SIDEREAL = 365.256363 d; OPH_YEAR_ANOMALISTIC = 365.259636 d; OPH_YEAR_IDEAL = 360 d ('the ideal year of the thesis'). periodDays holds the tropical value.
clocks.description: Year-length constants; OPH_YEAR_IDEAL = 360 is the ideal year of the thesis (the Draconian year of 360 turnings in v2).

openQuestions: YEAR CONVENTION: all 'year' fields are ASTRONOMICAL years exactly as the sources' JS uses them: 1 BC = 0, 2 BC = -1, so BC year B -> 1 - B (e.g. 5239 BC = -5238, 3113 BC = -3112, 2239 BC = -2238). Source: TIME MODEL comment, chronicon-clocks-calendrics.txt:484 / Chronicon_Engine_v2.html:639. fmtYear(a) = a<=0 ? (1-a)+' BC' : a+' CE'.

'YEAR ONE' (3895 BC, astro -3894) evaluates to AM 0 under AM = astro + 3894; ledger rows before it have negative AM (-5238 -> AM -1344). Source labels it Year One; 20-chronicon-source.md §7.7 reads AM as years elapsed.

Nibiru: absent from all assigned files. Outside them it appears in chronicon-desk/package.json (description only), Chronotecture-Charts/redesign/vid.html:111-112 ('Anunnaki planet Nibiru passes over ecliptic, entering' 1254; 'Nibiru seen from Earth as it exits the system' 1314) and iic.html:131 (1314 'Nibiru passed close to Earth'). 1254 and 1314 are Nemesis X ledger years; no source states Nibiru = Nemesis X. Not imported.

Sothic: v2 uses 1460 (mod(astro-139,1460), epoch astro 139); MANUAL OPH_SOTHIC = 1461. 20-chronicon-source.md §2.7 says Sothic/Saros/Inex/Jupiter-Saturn are absent from the clocks txt and have no Chronicon provenance (they are Natorion equation constants).
Precession: MANUAL OPH_PRECESSION = 25772 yr; v2 prose says '72 years — one precessional degree' (which x360 would be 25920). No precession clock/epoch in any source.
Saros, Inex, Jupiter-Saturn, planetary returns and year-length constants have no epoch, so no position/next-date can be computed from the sources alone.
